cultural.vision_reason: A Safavid-period Persian courtly miniature painting depicting a princess in fine dress within illuminated borders, with a Persian verse text on the verso — clearly Persian court art matching the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: Princess with Wine Bottle and Cup (recto); Persian Verses (verso)
physical.medium_raw: opaque watercolor, ink, and gold on paper
physical.summary: Single-page depictions of courtly figures became popular in Iran during the 1500s. The subject here conveys Safavid ideals of female beauty. Long dark hair falls in jeweled braids down to her ankles, while shorter tendrils frame her full, smooth face. She is shown in the three-quarter profile favored in Persian painting. The contrasting colors of the bright blue of her robe and the orange of her sash and tunic beneath are features of Safavid fashion.

location.made_in_place: Iran, Qazvin or Isfahan, Safavid period (1501-1722) (recto); Iran, possibly Timurid period (1370-1501) (verso)
